why: The inserted core principle forbidding cuts inside multi-character named entities/transliterations/fixed technical terms made the model avoid splitting names and parentheticals, giving small overall gains (largest in the shortest bin ≤3) by preserving those spans, but it also pushed cuts around parentheses, colons and quotation marks (moving cuts earlier or after parentheticals) and so created many regressions where punctuation or reporting verbs became isolated.
lesson: When protecting multi-token names/terms, don't force cuts that isolate punctuation, colons/quotes, or reporting verbs—avoid moving cuts so the left fragment becomes a dangling or unentailed piece.
